subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Age of Exploration Ships
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Age of Exploration Ships usable.

hook.text: Columbus crossed the Atlantic in a ship smaller than a modern tennis court. It took 36 days.

buildup.text: Caravels and carracks were nimble enough for ocean swells but sturdy enough to survive storms.

discovery.text: Lateen sails let ships sail closer to the wind. Square sails gave speed downwind. Crews used both.

twist.text: These ships carried tiny crews—about 40 men—crammed into spaces with no sanitation.

climax.text: Despite miserable conditions, these vessels connected continents and reshaped world history.

punchline.text: Tiny ships launched the age of global connection.

quiz.question: What advantage did lateen sails give exploration ships?
options: The ability to sail closer to the wind
